subject: prometheus-prometheus-18081
note: STANDING sample — chosen once. Grade it blind (relabelled, mixed with live clusters) on every grading day that touches this subject, and record the result with judge_stability.py --calibration. Do not re-draw: a fresh draw confounds sampling with drift.

clusters.summary: NewChildWithStepTracking allocates two numSteps-sized []int64 per subquery, sized by unvalidated subquery resolution, where NewChild allocated none
samplesRead is named and documented as an I/O count but increments once per step per series, so it over-counts memoized reads
The new test table encodes the double-count as expected values, so the tests lock the defect in rather than catch it
Whether slice aliasing across the reused evaluation buffer is a Go-semantics hazard
querySamplesRead.Add fires in the defer for failed, cancelled and timed-out queries, adding partial counts

The subquery attribution loop's design choices ship with only a fragment of rationale: nothing records why ceiling rather than floor, why out-of-window steps are clamped rather than dropped, that the clamp is load-bearing against an out-of-bounds write, or the intended sum invariant
The test file's PHASE banners are unusable as an index: the PHASE 3 banner appears twice over different content and no PHASE 1 banner exists
The "after last outer step" clamp is dead code under the test suite
New doc comments use different wording from the sibling helpers
Test expectations were captured from the implementation output rather than derived, and an IMPLEMENTATION NOTES scratch block admitting they may need refinement shipped with them
No test asserts the invariants SamplesRead <= TotalSamples or SamplesRead == sum(SamplesReadPerStep)
The four new exported helpers have no direct tests
Whether web UI types need updating
countSamplesAfter returns int64 while its same-file sibling returns int, forcing a cast at the combining call site
